Based on the recommendations, SCERT developed Prioritised Content for all classes with the help of SCERT and DIET faculty members and teachers through online mode which could be completed in the truncated academic year of 2020-21. As per the BPL survey conducted in ULBs during the year 2015 by Commissionerate of Municipal Administration for the implementation of Urban Poverty Alleviation Scheme the urban poor constitute nearly 38% of the total population.

2. Objectives and Goals

The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance livelihood opportunities in the urban areas by providing or enabling employment to every household whose adult members seek to do_ unskilled, semiskilled and skilled work. Creation of infrastructure, such as natural resource management works, flood mitigation works and the works for protection of the environment and greening of urban space; increasing urban consumption expenditure; promoting social and gender equity; and empowerment of women are important supplementary objectives. i) Improving Livelihood and Social Security by increasing employment opportunities.

ii) Facilitating employment opportunities appropriate to the skill levels.

iii) | Creation and maintenance of Public Assets.

iv) Greening and protection of the environment.

v) Undertaking works related to natural resource management.

in 7 Regions (7 Municipalities) and one Town Panchayat each in 37 Districts (37 Town Panchayats) in Tamil Nadu during the year 2021-22.

Imparting education has become easier and much more interesting than before in schools, with technological advancements. 2.8.3.Educational Management Information System (EMIS)

Education Management Information System is the digital backbone of the School Education Department wherein the information of every

school, teacher and student in Government, Government aided and private schools is maintained on a real time basis. It helps the Government in taking data driven policy decisions. The data of EMIS rests on three key pillars – student data, staff data and school data. All the data related to these three pillars are provided by the Headmasters through the EMIS portal through an exclusive login provided to each school. Each of the administrative officers at Block, Educational District, Revenue District and the state level is provided a separate login through which they can key-in inputs, view reports and access dashboards for monitoring, tracking and compliance purposes.

Unique Identity number has been assigned to each student and the same is carried forward throughout the period of schooling of the student thereby making it easy to track the student and his / her performance in various activities. All welfare schemes provided to students are also tagged to this unique ID of students, making the distribution more accountable and transparent.

Appointment and transfer counselling of teaching and non-teaching staff are carried out

Nominal roll preparation plays a vital role in the conduct of Board Examinations for Classes 10, 11 and 12. This has been made online through EMIS and the integration of data with Directorate of Government Examinations (DGE) has helped reduce administrative work.

Section Officer

ANNEXURE

Guidelines for the Implementation of Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam (KNMT)

1. Introduction

In Tamil Nadu, there are 14 Corporations (except Greater Chennai Corporation), 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats. Many schemes taken up in the recent years such as Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT are aimed at improving the infrastructure facilities of Corporations and major towns alone. Smart Cities Mission is being implemented only in 11 Corporations. AMRUT is also being implemented in 28 Towns only. The coverage of schemes in Corporations is relatively high when compared to Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Hence it has been decided to introduce a new Scheme “Kalaignar Nagarpura Mempattu Thittam”’(KNMT) in all 121 Municipalities and 528 Town Panchayats so as to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in these Urban Local

Bodies. 2. Implementation Plan

The vision of the Government is providing water service connection to all urban house holds, safe sewer disposal to each household either through UGSS or through FSTP, street lights and good road facilities. Though there are schemes for the provision of 100% functional household tap connections, sewer links, roads, such are highly capital intensive, mostly covering only prominent areas in the Urban Local Bodies. Infrastructure gaps remain existing in many backward areas/ slums and also newly added areas of the Municipalities and Town Panchayats. Considering the above factors, it has been decided to give preference to the slum areas/ backward areas and added areas of the ULBs for the implementation of KNMT.

2.1 Urban Development Plan (UDP)

The distribution of basic amenities is not uniform across the Urban Local Bodies and in certain wards / specific areas, the basic amenities are still inadequate. In order to have an equitable distribution of basic amenities, a detailed survey will be conducted and an Urban Development Plan (UDP) will be prepared for each urban local body so as to assess the present availability of basic infrastructure and the gaps

to be fulfilled.

The detailed survey will be conducted ward wise, with respect to the availability of water supply, sanitation, internal roads, street lights,

burial ground / crematorium availability and other community infrastructure. With regard to roads, a detailed Roads Network Plan will be prepared indicating all the major roads maintained by various agencies viz National Highways, State Highways and Municipalities / Town Panchayats (Access roads and internal streets) in the Urban Local Bodies concerned. With respect to water supply, the total demand, including the present supply and the future requirement will be taken into account and incorporated. Based on this, a “City Water balance Plan” will be prepared for each Urban Local Body. Similar survey and assessment of the gaps will be undertaken for all needed components of the ULBs concerned.
